JUDGMENT
This petition under Section 166 MV Act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 03-07-2023 about 11.00 a.m., petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing No.KL-44-G-3389 and one Ananda was riding the same near Thammasandra Gate, Bengaluru-Kanakapura road, Harohalli hobli and taluk, Ramanagara, at that time, the driver of Mahindra Thar Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MB-3906 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle)
drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle.
As a result, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and immediately he was taken to CDSIMER hospital, Harohalli, wherein he was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
It is submitted that he has spent a sum of 5,00,000/- towards his medical and other incidental expenses.

At the time of accident he was aged 19 years, he was studying 1st year B.Sc. Nursing at Dayananda Sagar University, Devarakaggalahalli, Harohalli and apart from this he was working in a Drugs and Chemist store, Harohalli and he was earning Rs.20,000/-p.m.
Due to the accident, he has not attended his classes and work, resulted loss of education and loss of income.
The accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, it is requested to award Rs.30,00,000/- from the Respondents.
3. In response to the petition notice, both the Respondents have appeared before the court through their counsels and filed their separate written statements.

4. The 1st Respondent-who is RC owner of the offending vehicle has admitted that he is the RC owner of the offending vehicle and it was insured with the Respondent No.2 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident and driver was holding valid DL.

Further he has denied that the alleged accident was caused, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and further contended that the accident was caused due to the negligence of rider of motorcycle, as he was riding the motorcycle carelessly and suddenly came across the car and accident occurred.
Further, he has denied the age, status of petitioner and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5. Respondent No.2 - insurer has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of offending vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident.
However, its liability is subject to terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
It has also contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further, it has contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid driving licence.

Further it has denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle and contended Amal Cyriac vs Srinivasan M P on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26245407/
2 that it was the negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle as he was riding the motorcycle in a zigzag manner, suddenly came on the lane of offending vehicle and without having DL not wearing helmet at the time of accident.

expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.
It is contended that the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries when he was pillion rider in motorcycle bearing No.KL-44-G- 3389 on 03-07-2023 about 11.00 a.m., near Thammasandra Gate, Bengaluru - Kanakapura Road, Harohalli Taluk, Ramanagara District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Mahindra Thar Jeep bearing No.KA-51- MB-3906?

2. What compensation Petitioner is entitled?
3. What order ?

doctor is examined as PW-2 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.20.
8.
The Respondents have not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.
9. I have heard the arguments of counsel for the Petitioner and respondents and have perused the material on record.

10. My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative. Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

Ramanagara, at that time, the driver of Mahindra Thar Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MB-3906 drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle.
As a result, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

sentences.text: In order to substantiate his case, petitioner has examined as PW-1 and got marked the police documents at Ex.P.1 to 9 i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, spot sketch, IMV report, wound certificate, notice, reply and charge sheet.
To support of his claim, Dr.Nagaraj B.N., Orthopedic surgeon is examined as PW-2 and he has produced the documents at Ex.P.19 and 20.
As per wound certificate he has sustained fracture of right femur at middle one third.

13. It is contended by the Respondent -insurance company that it was the negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle as he was riding the motorcycle in a zigzag manner, suddenly came on the lane of offending vehicle and thereby accident occurred.
The rider of motorcycle was not having DL and were not wearing helmet at the time of accident.
During the cross examination he has put forth the said suggestions, however, PW1 denied the same.
Except these suggestion, there are no materials to show that the accident has not occurred due to negligence driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
14. The Police have filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle after through investigation and the same has not been challenged by any one.
All the evidence and materials clearly indicates that it was negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.
All the materials show that accident was caused due to the negligence of driver of the offending vehicle.
The Petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.2 :- As per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained fracture of right femur at middle one third and it is grievous in nature.
Due to the accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was taken to CDSIMER Dr.Chandramma Dayananda Sagar hospital, Harohalli, wherein, he was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery.

Due to the accidental injuries he could not attend his classes and exam and also his work and has suffered loss of income.
He has lost his normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.

Orthopedic surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dentral Center, Bengaluru, has deposed that the Petitioner has sustained right femur fracture in a RTA and he was treated with CRIF with IMIL nailing was done.

On examination he has assessed the total disability of right lower limb at 47% and to the whole body physical disability at 16%.
17. On careful reading of evidence of PW-2 makes it clear that PW-2 has not treated the Petitioner.
During the course of cross examination they denied that he has assessed disability on the higher side.
It is pertinent to note that PW-2 has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.

Therefore, considering that the grievous injuries is on the leg and considering the Amal Cyriac vs Srinivasan M P on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26245407/
4 difficulties and evidence of PW-2 and also by considering the age of the Petitioner, the functional disability is assessed at 10%.

sentences.text: In the petition, the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 19 years.

Wherein Ex.P.14 Aadhar card shows that he was born on 15-05-2004, the same is considered as age of the deceased as on the date of accident as 19 years and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 18.
19.
The age of the petitioner is 19 years as on the date of accident.
Due to the accident he has sustained grievous injuries.
He was admitted in CDSIMER hospital at Harohalli.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was student of 1st year B.Sc. and apart from this he working in a drug and chemist store at Harohalli and was earning Rs.20,000/-P.M.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do attend the classes, his work and is unable to concentrate on his studies and to do his work as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documents to substantiate his income.

In the absence of material with regard to source of income,
the tribunal has to be considered the notional income chart of the Lok Adalath.
20. On perusal of the record, it appears that the age of the petitioner as on date of the alleged accident was about 19 years.
The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs.16,000/- Per Month.

Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
21. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability:
Looking into the nature of injuries, it definitely affects the working capacity of any person.

As the Petitioner is a student cum working,
considering nature of injury and doctor's evidence the total functional disability of the Petitioner is considered at 10%.

Thus loss of future income comes to Rs.16,000 x 12 x 18 x 10/100=
Rs.3,45,600/- towards loss of future income.
22. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has sustained head injuries and was inpatient for a period of 16 days which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .40,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
23. Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to suffer in his day today activities and face hardships.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .25,000/- under loss of amenities of life.
24. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.12.
After through calculation, the amount all medical bills is Rs.2,08,796/-.
The Respondent has not disputed the medical bills and the bills appears to be genuine.

Hence, Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.2,08,796/-
towards Medical Expenses.

sentences.text: Future medical expenses: PW-2 has stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants which will cost Rs.60,000/- .
But he has not produced any estimation report.
In the absence of material evidence, it is just and reasonable to award Rs.15,000/- towards future medical expenses.
26. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges: Ex

& 11 -Discharge summaries show that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at CDSIMER hospital, Harohalli from 03-07- 2023 to 08-07-2023 & at Caritas hospital, Kottayam, Kerala from 08-07-2023 to 18-07-2023 i.e, totally for a period of 16 days.

Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .20,000/-
under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.

27. Loss of earning during laid up period: With regard to loss of earnings during treatment,
considering 16 days admission in the hospital as inpatient.
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.17 - sick leave certificate from 3-7-2023 to 4-12-2023, but he has not produced any documents to show that he has lost his academic year.
This has not been disputed by the Respondent.
Therefore, around 3 months for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for 3 months.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .16,000 x 3 = Rs.48,000/-.
28.

Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:

ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.

p.a. (except future medical expenses) from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
